text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Bulgaria's central government budget deficit rose by some 39 billion levs in the second half of April to 330.18 billion levs mainly due to interest and discount payments on government securities.
-- Bulgarian National Bank governor Lyubomir Filipov said he was prepared to step down once parliament decided whom to appoint as his successor to run the bank under a currency board system.

-- The State Savings Bank, Bulgaria's largest savings institution, will lower interest rates in line with the new central bank main interest rate of 5.2 percent monthly, bankers said. Monthly interest on one-month deposits will be 3.15 percent and annual interest on credits to individuals will be 67 percent.
-- Bulgaria's Privatisation Agency opened a procedure for the sell-off of 75 percent of the country's largest oil refinery Neftochim.

-- Bulgaria will not use a credit line under the U.S. GSM-102 programme for wheat imports and will probably opt for purchasing cheaper wheat from Hungary instead, Agriculture Minister Roumen Hristov said. The price of Hungarian grain was about $190 per tonne while imports from the U.S. would be made at $210 per tonne at least, he said.
-- Prices of petrol and diesel fuel were not expected to change after the interim cabinet liberalised prices because the lev/dollar exchange rate is stable, experts from the Neftochim refinery said.

-- Bulgaria's President Petar Stoyanov was expected to ask the leader of pro-reform Union of Democratic Forces (UDF) Ivan Kostov to form the country's new government on Wednesday, the leader of the UDF parliamentary group said. The UDF won an absolute majority in parliament at the April 19 election.

-- Bulgaria's Privatisation Agency has launched a check into the sale of the Pleven-based oil refinery Plama to Euroenergy Holding after the buyer failed to begin repayment of the refinery's debts agreed under the sale contract, Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Bozhkov said.

-- The World Bank has approved a $40 million loan to Bulgaria for imports of essential goods like grain, fuel and medical supplies. The loan is part of a $290 million funding package earmarked for Bulgaria if the government speeds up privatisation of state factories and banks and eliminates public sector losses. -- Sofia Newsroom +359-2 981 4145
